newsitem.title: GERMANY: Telekom settles into life on the Frankfurt bourse.
newsitem.headline: Telekom settles into life on the Frankfurt bourse.

text.p: Shares in German telecommunications giant Deutsche Telekom have passed their first few hectic days on the Frankfurt bourse with flying colours, dealers said on Thursday, as early profit-taking on the stock receded and trade normalised.
"It has been a great success," said one trader of Europe's biggest-ever initial public offering of $13 billion.
Telekom shares ended Thursday floor dealings up 35 pfennigs, over one percent, at 32.15 marks and dealers said most speculative investors, mainly foreigners, had stopped taking profit on the stock.
"International investors sold quickly. The Anglo-Saxon way of dealing is simply more cold blooded," said one dealer.
A third of the Telekom issue was placed abroad and traders said the temptation to take profit on an investment which gave a quick and attractive return was too great to resist.
Shares in Telekom started frenetic trade on Monday at a price of 33.20 marks, representing an immediate premium of 16.5 percent on the 28.50 mark issue price.

But dealers said not all international investors had done a quick hit and run on Telekom. "The weighting of Telekom in the DAX (German index of top shares) and other indices means fund managers must have some in their portfolios," said one trader.
German institutional and private investors had been keener to hold onto their shares than their foreign counterparts.

"Around 95 percent of our customers who bought shares in Deutsche Telekom are still Telekom shareholders," said Tessen von Heydebreck, Deutsche Bank management board member, with responsibility for private customers.

Some dealers said German investors were conforming to their traditional reputation of long-termism, but others said they were just keen to cash in on the benefits of attractive dividends offered by the firm.
Telekom has forecast a dividend per share of 60 pfennigs for 1996 and 1.20 marks for next year.

"It would be really bad for the share price if the company does not stick to its dividend forecast. But as long as it holds onto that the share price should be well-supported at 30 marks," said one dealer.
Dealers said they expected Telekom shares to trade in a band between 31 and 33 marks in the coming weeks. They said any climb up to 34 marks would be treated as a fresh opportunity to take profit.
On Monday the stock touched a high of 34.10 marks, while on Wednesday and Thursday profit pushed the stock down almost seven percent to a low of 31.75 marks.

Well over one hundred million shares changed hands in the first three days of trade in Telekom in Frankfurt. Dealings in the stock also sent waves through the New York and Tokyo exchanges, where Telekom was also listed for the first time this week.
But dealers said dealings were now calming down, with less than 10 million shares traded on Thursday in Frankfurt. "Today was the first day of normal trade for Telekom," said one dealer.
The Frankfurt stock exchange said IBIS computerised dealings would return to normal trading hours next week after having been extended for two hours to accommodate heavy extra volume in Telekom.
Dealers said they had been disappointed with volumes in the extra hours.
"Extending the hours brought nothing," said one trader, "There has been no customer demand and some evenings I did not get a single call."
